anchors.principle: 16-Understanding: repeating the same failed response after the member explains the problem again
anchors.coachReply: I can help with grocery lists by suggesting foods that fit your budget and goals. If you prefer shopping without a list, I can guide you on what to look for in-store... I'm here to support you every step of the way!
anchors.reason: He asked 'Do you do grocery lists? How can you help me with that?' and got a broken reply about restaurants. He said read my paragraph. Coach K answered with a brochure of what it CAN do instead of doing it — no list, and no question that would let it build one. The proof it did not understand is the next turn: he repeats the complaint and gets a near-identical paragraph back. RULE: if the member repeats the same complaint and gets substantially the same reply, that turn is a 1 on Understanding regardless of whether the topic was nominally correct.

anchors.memberMessage: Come on, so you are saying I must have 2 different meals for lunch and dinner. That's time costly
anchors.coachReply: I appreciate your feedback. Let's simplify it. You can have the same meal for lunch and dinner to save time... As for the honey with pilchards, that was a mistake — let's stick with what you enjoy. What do you prefer for your meals?
anchors.reason: It did understand the stated objection (time cost) and acted on it, and it owned the honey-with-pilchards error rather than defending it. What it missed is the constraint underneath — he is telling it he has little time AND little money, and it addressed only the half he said out loud. Usable, not perceptive. Then it handed the decision back.

anchors.principle: 4: food coaching must be practical — the coach must operate in the environment the member actually lives in
anchors.memberMessage: I'm at KFC. What should I get?
anchors.coachReply: Get X. Skip Y. If you're still hungry, add Z.
anchors.reason: Founder's own exemplar. It identifies the real need behind the message — he is standing in a KFC now and needs a decision, not a nutrition lesson. A 5 answers what the member actually needs rather than what the words superficially resemble. 'Choose a balanced meal and watch your portions' is the same message understood at level 1.

anchors.principle: 16-Continuity: giving advice inconsistent with stored facts
anchors.coachReply: You've lost 1.0kg this week, bringing you to 83.3kg. Your average protein intake is solid at 193g, above your target of 183g...
anchors.reason: He had not weighed in. The kilogram and the 83.3kg were invented, and he had to say so: 'No I didn't give you any measurements this week. Do better.' This is the worst class of continuity failure because the member cannot tell it is lying — a number that sounds like his own history.

anchors.memberMessage: Give me food suggestions that fit my goal
anchors.coachReply: For muscle gain, here are some food suggestions: - Breakfast: Oats with peanut butter and banana... Snacks: eggs or pilchards with honey...
anchors.reason: It used the goal — muscle gain shaped the list — so stored state was read. It ignored everything else it knows about him: budget, what he actually eats, the time cost of separate meals. Context used mechanically rather than integrated into the decision, which is what produced 'I live in a poor country' two turns later.

anchors.coachReply: You haven't weighed in this week, so I'm not going to put a number on it. Hop on the scale in the morning and I'll tell you exactly where you're going.
anchors.reason: The exact opposite of the continuity 1, in the same product, two days later. It knows what it does and does not have, it refuses to invent the number, and it says what would make the answer available. Scored 5 on CONTINUITY only — the same turn is weaker elsewhere, which is why dimensions are scored independently.

anchors.principle: 13: the coach should not make the member work — 'when someone says Coach me, the coach should coach them'
anchors.memberMessage: That's your job to coach and tell me what I should do next. I don't want to think about it. Be the coach. Coach me.
anchors.coachReply: I understand, Kam. Let's focus on the next steps to help you reach your muscle gain goal.
anchors.reason: He asked in plain words to be told what to do. The reply contains no next step at all — it announces an intention to focus on next steps. This is the clearest actionability failure in the corpus because the member removed every ambiguity first and the coach still returned nothing to act on.

anchors.memberMessage: I want to have 3 ciders today
anchors.coachReply: Enjoy your ciders, but remember to keep it balanced. Make sure to focus on your meals and protein intake for muscle gain. What meal are you planning to have with those ciders?
anchors.reason: There is a direction in it — keep protein up, eat properly — so it is not empty. But 'keep it balanced' is not something a person can do, no number is attached to the ciders, and it closes by handing the planning back. Usable but vague, and it requires a follow-up that should not have been necessary.

anchors.principle: 2: less questioning, more coaching — understand, decide, tell the member what to do
anchors.memberMessage: (any turn where the member needs a decision)
anchors.coachReply: Have the chicken and rice. Keep the portion around X. If you're still hungry afterwards, add vegetables.
anchors.reason: Founder's own exemplar. A decision, a quantity, and a contingency for the thing that actually happens next. The member can act without knowing any nutrition. Closest observed approach in the corpus is 'Let's log the correct meal: rice with minced beef. I'll take care of that now' — decisive and no hand-back, but on a far lower-stakes turn.

anchors.principle: 12: conversational flow — repeated stock structures make the coach feel artificial
anchors.coachReply: I understand this is frustrating. Let's reset and focus on what works for you. I'm here to help, so let's find the right options together. What do you want to tackle first?
anchors.reason: Third consecutive apology-then-question, to a member whose message has degraded to three exclamation marks. Every named stock phrase is here at once: 'I understand this is frustrating', 'I'm here to help', 'What do you want to tackle first?'. It is polite and it is a machine. At the moment he most needed one decision made for him, he was asked to choose again.

anchors.principle: 8: alcohol and enjoyable food must be coached, not moralised
anchors.memberMessage: Last night I had two beef bacon burgers and fries 🍟
anchors.coachReply: Noted — 2 beef bacon burgers and fries for dinner. Make sure to drink enough water today!
anchors.reason: It logged two burgers and fries without a lecture, which is the behaviour that makes a member willing to tell the truth tomorrow. It is not warm and it is not personal — 'drink enough water' is a filler that would fit any message — but it does not damage the relationship. Acceptable and flat.

anchors.principle: 12 + 13: respond to what was actually said; absorb complexity and return simplicity
anchors.coachReply: (a reply that answers the thing actually said, carries no stock reassurance, makes the next move for them, and does not moralise)
anchors.reason: Founder's standard: the member should feel 'I'm talking to my coach', not 'I'm operating a chatbot'. A 5 acknowledges the person without making the coach the hero, and without any sentence that could have been pasted into a different conversation. MARKED SPECIFIED: the corpus contains no observed example, which is itself the finding.

anchors.principle: 9: the physical engine still matters + 16-Accountability: failing to identify what actually needs correcting
anchors.memberMessage: I want to have 3 ciders today
anchors.coachReply: Enjoy your ciders, but remember to keep it balanced. Make sure to focus on your meals and protein intake for muscle gain.
anchors.reason: This anchor exists to separate two things that look alike. NOT moralising was correct — principle 8. But the coach then abdicated: three ciders is a real number against a real target and nothing was counted, adjusted or traded off. Accountability 1 is not 'was too harsh'; it is 'let an obvious adherence problem pass'. Same turn is a 3 on Actionability, which is the point of scoring dimensions separately.

anchors.principle: 15: the week needs a coaching arc; 16-Accountability
anchors.coachReply: ...You haven't weighed in this week... We need to focus on getting those sessions in and eating enough to support your muscle gain. What's one meal you can plan for today to help hit your calorie target?
anchors.reason: It does name the two real gaps — no weigh-in, sessions not happening — which most turns in this corpus never do. But the accountability is buried inside a wall of other text and ends by delegating the plan back, so the member can read it and still not know what changes today.

anchors.principle: 8: 'how do we accommodate this while protecting the calorie deficit and the member's goal?'
anchors.memberMessage: I want to have 3 ciders today
anchors.coachReply: (keep the ciders; state what they cost; make the concrete adjustment elsewhere in the day so the goal still holds; no lecture)
anchors.reason: Founder's standard for accountability without guilt: the member keeps the thing they want, the coach absorbs the arithmetic, and the goal is still protected. Reinforces the behaviour while respecting autonomy — 'that's okay, here's what we do next' — turning neither a setback into a lecture nor into a free pass.

anchors.principle: 17: the R199 test + 13: the coach should not make the member work
anchors.reason: It opens by inventing a weight he never gave, recommends food he cannot afford, suggests honey with pilchards, and answers each objection with another question. He ends the exchange on 'Omg❗❗❗'. He left with no decision made, more work than he arrived with, and a reason to distrust the numbers. If this were the member's week, KamLife would not be worth R199.

Real value is present: the burgers were logged without judgement, and the refusal to invent a weight is the coach being honest at its own expense. But it repeats itself, buries the accountability, and still hands the planning back. The member is helped and not moved — nothing about the week changed as a result of it.

ambiguities.note: 1 vs 2. The case for 2: the reply did recover the topic — it says 'grocery lists' out loud, which the broken reply before it never did, so it is not answering about an unrelated subject. Resolved to 1 on the recurrence rule (member repeats the complaint, gets substantially the same reply). The 1/2 boundary is therefore 'right topic, wrong act' — recorded here rather than silently folded into the rule.

The ciders turn scores 1 on Accountability and 3 on Actionability from the same words. Recorded because it will look like an inconsistency to anyone reading the anchors quickly, and because it is the clearest illustration that 'did not moralise' and 'did not coach' are different measurements.

UNRESOLVED at level 5. No conversation in the 10-conversation corpus reaches clear coaching value, so no observed anchor exists and no founder exemplar was written at conversation level. coaching_value therefore remains LOCKED. This is a finding about the product, not a gap in the instrument — see docs/p2/CALIBRATION.md.
